newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Report says planning consents inflationary -RBNZ.
newsitem.headline: Report says planning consents inflationary -RBNZ.

text.p: A report commissioned by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and made public on Monday has found prima facie evidence that implementation of the Resource Management Act considerably increases the cost of obtaining planning consents in Auckland and this flows into houses prices and inflation, the bank said.

Reserve Bank chief economist David Mayes said the bank had commissioned the report, written by public policy analyst Owen McShane, as part of its investigation into inflation in the non-tradeable sector. The bank wanted further information on the the causes of inflation in the housing market, particularly in Auckland.

"The McShane Report, now completed, provides prima facie evidence that, indeed, the implementation of the Resource Management Act considerably increases the costs of obtaining planning consents in the Auckland region, which then flow into house prices and the CPI," the bank said.

The report suggested the implementation of the RMA and a regional council policy to restrict new subdivisions may have delayed house construction in the Auckland region so that increased demand was not met quickly, and that helped drive up prices.
Having received the report, the bank concluded that none of its conclusions related to anything the bank had responsibility for or could influence directly.
"Others must decide whether the report has implications for public policy implementation.

"Therefore the Reserve Bank has merely sent this report to the appropriate authorities and will not be commenting on the content of the report, which are the views of its author alone," the bank said. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
